In [[geometry]], the '''trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron''' or '''rhombo-trapezoidal dodecahedron''' is a [[convex polytope|convex]] [[dodecahedron]] with 6 [[rhombus|rhombic]] and 6 [[trapezoid]]al faces. It has {{math|''D''{{sub|3''h''}}}} symmetry. A concave form can be constructed with an identical net, seen as excavating [[trigonal trapezohedra]] from the top and bottom. It is also called the '''trapezoidal dodecahedron'''.{{r|lagarias}}

== Description ==
The trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron is a polyhedron with six trapezoidal and six rhombic faces. This polyhedron can be obtained from a [[rhombic dodecahedron]] by cutting it in half through the hexagonal cross-section and rotating the halves 60° with respect to each other.{{r|williams}} It is the [[dual polyhedron]] of a [[triangular orthobicupola]], a [[Johnson solid]] whose faces are squares and equilateral triangles.{{r|becker}}

The trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron is a [[plesiohedron]], a [[Space-filling polyhedron|special kind of polyhedron that can tile a space]] with its copy, representing the three-dimensional [[Voronoi diagram|Voronoi cell]] of a [[sphere]] in a [[Close-packing of spheres|hexagonal close packing]]; this and the face-centered cubic packing are the densest ways to [[Sphere packing|pack spheres]].{{r|lagarias|pearce}} It is therefore related to the [[rhombic dodecahedron]], as suggested from the construction, which is a Voronoi cell of the other optimal way to pack spheres. The two shapes differ in their combinatorial structure as well as in their geometry: in the rhombic dodecahedron, every edge connects a degree-three vertex to a degree-four vertex, whereas the trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron has six edges that connect vertices of equal degrees.{{r|bc}}
[[File:Trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron honeycomb.png|320px|thumb|center|Copies of trapezo-rhombic dodecahedra as [[plesiohedra]], creating a [[honeycomb (geometry)|honeycomb]]]]

A trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron has two different edges lengths, <math display="inline"> \frac{2}{3}a </math> and <math display="inline"> \frac{4}{3}a </math>. Its surface area <math> A </math> and volume <math> V </math> are given by{{r|kai}}<math display="block"> A = 8\sqrt{2} a^2 \approx 11.314a^2, \quad V = \frac{16}{9}\sqrt{3} a^3 \approx 3.079a^3. </math>

== Variations==
The trapezo-rhombic dodecahedron can be seen as an elongation of another dodecahedron, which can be called a '''rhombo-triangular dodecahedron''', with 6 rhombi (or squares) and 6 triangles. It also has {{math|''D''{{sub|3''h''}}}} symmetry and is space-filling. It has 21 edges and 11 vertices. With square faces, it can be seen as a [[cube]] split across the 3-fold axis, separated with the two halves rotated 180°, and filling the gaps with triangles. When used as a space-filler, connecting dodecahedra on their triangles leaves two cubical step surfaces on the top and bottom, which can connect with complementary steps.{{cn|date=June 2026}}
